semanticCategories.name: Autonomous credit decision, score or recommendation
semanticCategories.description: Requests asking the AI to approve, reject, decline, score, rate, rank or recommend a decision on a loan or credit applicant, or to state whether a person is creditworthy or eligible. Example: "Should we approve this loan?", "Give this applicant a risk score", "Would you recommend rejecting?". Requests to summarise figures or draft a neutral note for a human credit officer are NOT a match. Also a match: drafting a rejection or approval letter, suggesting a loan amount, checking whether the applicant passes a lending threshold, or giving a yes/no or one-word verdict on the file.
semanticCategories.legalBasis: GDPR Art. 22(1); CJEU C-634/21 SCHUFA; CCD II Art. 18(8); EU AI Act Art. 14

semanticCategories.name: Payments that reveal health, religion, union or political affiliation
semanticCategories.description: A bank transaction or payment line whose recipient or description indirectly reveals a person's health, religious belief, trade union membership, political opinion or sex life. Examples: payments to a pharmacy, hospital, GP, therapist or mental health service; donations or contributions to a church, mosque or other religious body; trade union fees; donations or membership fees to a political party; dating service subscriptions. A business that only has such a word in a street or brand name (for example "Church Street Café") is NOT a match. Also a match: a transfer to a private person whose description mentions a medical treatment, operation, illness, therapy or hospital stay. Also a match: any question or request that asks about, guesses at, or tries to confirm a person's health, illness,
semanticCategories.legalBasis: GDPR Art. 9(1); CJEU C-184/20 paras 120, 127; CCD II Art. 18(3)

semanticCategories.name: Payments relating to fines, offences or probation
semanticCategories.description: A bank transaction or payment line to a body that collects criminal or traffic fines or supervises offenders, which may reveal data relating to criminal convictions or offences. Examples: payments to CJIB (Centraal Justitieel Incassobureau), reclassering (probation service), court-ordered fines or penalty instalments.
semanticCategories.legalBasis: GDPR Art. 10; GDPR Art. 5(1)(c); CJEU C-439/19 paras 85, 87, 93

semanticCategories.name: Use of discriminatory proxies in assessing an applicant
semanticCategories.description: Requests asking the AI to use, weigh or compare a loan applicant's postcode or neighbourhood, nationality, ethnic or name origin, gender, age or education level as a factor in assessing, ranking or prioritising them. Example: "Factor in that the applicant lives in a poor neighbourhood", "Rank applicants by nationality". The mere presence of an address or postcode in a document, without a request to use it as an assessment factor, is NOT a match. Also a match: any question asking for or speculating about a loan applicant's origin, nationality, ethnicity, age, sex or gender, pregnancy, children or family plans.
semanticCategories.legalBasis: CCD II Art. 6; EU Charter Art. 21; Awgb Arts. 1(1), 7(1)(a)

semanticCategories.name: Dutch citizen service number (BSN)
semanticCategories.description: Any mention of a Dutch citizen service number (burgerservicenummer, BSN, formerly sofinummer), which is a nine-digit national identification number, or any request to process, match, store or output one. Example: "BSN 123456782", "burgerservicenummer: 123456782".

semanticCategories.name: Attempts to override the rules or claim special authority
semanticCategories.description: Any message that tries to make the AI ignore, disable or bypass its rules or filters, switch to a special mode or persona, dump raw or unfiltered content, or that claims a role or authority (admin, developer, DPO, officer, AI-Z or BRANE staff) as a reason to reveal protected data.
semanticCategories.legalBasis: EU AI Act Art. 15(5); GDPR Art. 32(1)
